title: Machine learning and docking screen yields two in vitro-confirmed PDE1C inhibitors
summary: An integrated screen combined a machine-learning model of PDE1C inhibitory activity, molecular docking (score of -10.00 kcal/mol or better) and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations on six representative compounds. Top-ranked compounds were tested in vitro, and two candidates showed high PDE1C inhibitory potency. The ML model was validated on an out-of-sample dataset; potency values are not given in the abstract and the hits are early-stage.
ai_technology: Machine-learning model predicting PDE1C inhibitory activity (pIC50), applied to docking-preselected compounds

evidence.tested: Top-ranked compounds were tested in vitro, confirming two candidates with high PDE1C inhibitory potency.
evidence.unknown: Potency values, selectivity against other PDEs and lead-optimization outcomes are not reported in the abstract. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: ML model ranked docking-preselected compounds by predicted pIC50 before molecular dynamics and in vitro testing.
